user.title: HVAC Schedule Optimizer
user.description: Pick the thermostat to schedule. If your indoor temperature comes from a separate sensor you trust more than the thermostat's own reading, add it too. Turn off any other scheduler (such as Climate Scheduler) for this thermostat so they do not fight.

abort.already_configured: This thermostat is already set up.

init.title: Comfort limits and schedule
init.description: Temperatures use your Home Assistant unit. The optimizer only proposes schedules that keep the house under these limits. The baseline is your current schedule, used for the savings comparison and as the starting schedule.

data.history_days: Days of history to learn from

data_description.room_sensors: Any number of indoor sensors. Each room learns how it runs compared with the thermostat (about 3 days of readings), then you choose when it counts against the comfort limits on the next page.
data_description.outdoor_sensors: Any number of outdoor sensors. Their median replaces Open-Meteo's past weather when learning, and corrects the forecast for your spot. One sensor in direct sun is outvoted when you have three or more.

rooms.title: When each room counts
rooms.description:
Choose when each room's temperature has to stay under the comfort limits: always, only during awake hours, only during sleep hours, or never (shown on the card only). The thermostat itself always counts.

{names}

fan.title: Fan
fan.description:
Your thermostat reports these fan modes: {modes}.

With fan control on, the optimizer can circulate the blower to even out rooms, but only once a room has learned what the fan does (about 4 hours of fan-only running in history) and only when it costs less than cooling the whole house harder. The fan always goes back to the normal mode when a fan window ends, when you pause the schedule, and when the integration unloads.

data.fan_control: Let the optimizer use the fan
data.fan_mode_normal: Normal mode (blower runs only with cooling)
data.fan_mode_circulate: Circulate mode (blower runs on its own)
data.fan_humidity_max: Do not circulate above this indoor humidity (%)

data_description.fan_watts: Variable speed blowers on circulate often draw 50 to 150 W; older single speed blowers 300 to 500 W.
data_description.ac_kw: Roughly 1 kW per ton of cooling. Used only to weigh blower time against AC time.
data_description.humidity_sensor: If empty, the thermostat's own humidity reading is used when it has one. Circulating right after cooling can blow moisture off the coil back into the house.

error.same_fan_mode: Normal and circulate have to be different fan modes.
